datum.name: Local mean sea level (the 3DEP DEM in Hawaii)
datum.source: NOAA CO-OPS Hilo 1617760 datums, 1983-2001 epoch: MSL 1.545 m, MLLW 1.196 m above station datum

tide.what: NOAA's harmonic prediction for Hilo that night: low 0.59 ft MLLW at 20:10, high 1.59 ft MLLW at 01:23 HST. The waves rode a weak high tide about 0.1 m above mean sea level.

waves.label: Wave 1
waves.heightNote: above normal water at the Wailuku River bridge (Eaton et al. 1961 p. 139)
waves.periodNote: NCEI runup 3922 and Lander & Lockridge 1989 give a 30 min period
waves.note: Wave 1 crest, about 4 ft above normal at the Wailuku River bridge

waves.label: Wave 2
waves.heightNote: above normal at the bridge; it flooded Kamehameha Ave and the business district
waves.periodNote: derived: interval from crest 1 (00:13) to crest 2 (00:46)
waves.note: Wave 2 crest, about 9 ft above normal; Kamehameha Ave and the bayfront flood

riseFrom.note: trough about 3 ft below normal at 00:30 (Eaton)

waves.label: Wave 3, the bore
waves.heightNote: maximum runup 35 ft (10.7 m) (Eaton et al. 1961; NCEI 3922); the bore front was about 20 ft at the bridge. Inland flooding uses Loomis's 18 measured 1960 runup heights
waves.periodNote: derived: interval from crest 2 (00:46) to the bore (01:04)
waves.boreSpeedNote: Scripps Institution of Oceanography press release (28 Oct 1960): about 20 miles an hour
waves.note: The bore comes ashore and runs inland at about 20 mph to the 1960 runup line

risingLimbNote: Between a published trough or start of rise and the next crest the water is assumed to rise linearly (derived, not measured).
